subject: Dedicated capacity minimum throughput ask — Orbitlytics
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@orbitlytics.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity minimum throughput ask — Orbitlytics

Hi Irene / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Orbitlytics is keen to move forward with Redwood Dedicated. Procurement raised a hard requirement we need to lock into the SOW: a documented minimum throughput guarantee for our reserved pool during defined peak windows.

Context: our recommender model has strict tail-latency sensitivity. We anticipate weekday peaks from 13:00–16:00 PST with sustained load ~6k req/min and short spikes to ~9k req/min (spikes up to 10 minutes). We want explicit behavior for preemption, queueing, and credits if throughput degrades below a firm floor.

Please confirm you can include language that defines:
- How "minimum throughput" is measured (completed inferences/min and the window used)
- Allowed preemption during maintenance and unplanned failure handling
- Crediting formula tied to magnitude/duration of shortfall
- Any exclusions during maintenance, incident remediation, or if we use burst pricing

Attached are our redlines for the SLA. Procurement is cc'd. Can you provide a written proposal by next Friday?

Best,
Sara Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Orbitlytics
Attachment: Orbitlytics_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf (summary: redlines around minimum throughput, credit caps, measurement windows)

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity minimum throughput ask — Orbitlytics

Quick technical read — current Dedicated behavior and a suggested operational spec:

Current behavior:
- Reserved pools are backed by pinned GPUs; under normal operations we do not evict customer workloads. Preemption happens only for scheduled maintenance or catastrophic failures.
- Queueing: per-GPU request queue depth is configurable; the platform applies smoothing (default 60s) for throughput observability.
- Burst handling: we route to spare capacity within region when available; otherwise requests queue and are admitted per rate-limiter.

Suggested commitments we can reasonably include:
1) Measurement: evaluate throughput using 5-minute sliding windows, reported as hourly aggregates to avoid penalizing transient drops.
2) Agreed floor: X completed inferences/min per A100-eq GPU * reserved_gpu_count. We should compute X after Orbitlytics shares model footprint and latency targets. Preliminary conservative value: 120 inferences/min per A100-eq GPU with p99 optimization offload.
3) Preemption allowance: <1% scheduled preemption with 72-hour notice. Unscheduled hardware failures follow failover runbook; if we cannot restore >=90% of floor within 30 minutes post-event, crediting can apply.
4) Crediting proposal: Credit = min((1 - (observed / agreed)) * shortfall_hours * monthly_fee, cap) with cap = 25% of monthly reserved fee.

Operational caveats: we need their model size, avg tokens/request, and p95/p99 latency goals to finalize X and any latency-oriented SLAs. Also recommend an optional p95 latency objective in the SLA for tail-sensitive workloads.

-David
David Kim
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity-modeling.csv

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity minimum throughput ask — Orbitlytics

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the redlines. We've reviewed with infra and legal and propose the following starting SLA language: 

Proposal summary:
- Agreed floor: Redwood will guarantee 120 completed inferences/min per A100-equivalent reserved GPU, multiplied by Orbitlytics' reserved GPU count. Final per-GPU value to be validated once Orbitlytics confirms model footprint and p95 target.
- Measurement: throughput evaluated via 5-minute sliding windows, aggregated hourly; credits trigger when hourly aggregate <95% of agreed floor.
- Preemption & maintenance: scheduled preemption <1% with 72-hour notice. Unscheduled hardware failure remediation target 30 minutes; if throughput remains <90% of floor after 30 minutes, credits apply.
- Credits: (1 - (observed / agreed)) * shortfall_duration_hours * proportional_monthly_commitment capped at 25% of the monthly reserved fee.
- Burst & smoothing: customers can purchase burst capacity; otherwise bursts are served via queueing and smoothing windows above.

Next steps: 1) Irene/David — confirm wording and add any operational limits for p99-sensitive cases; 2) Sara — if acceptable in principle, we will prepare a DocuSign with the SLA appendix for signature (draft link included). Happy to set a call Monday to walk procurement through the credit math.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_proposal_summary_for_Orbitlytics.pdf

- Orbitlytics will share model footprint by EOD Tuesday.
- Procurement would prefer the credit cap be expressed as a waiverable amount (e.g., "standard cap 25% but negotiable to 35% for multi-year commitments") — can you phrase that?
- For measurement, can we add a clause that excludes pre-announced maintenance windows and region-level outages beyond Redwood's control (e.g., cloud provider network events)?

If you can send an updated SLA appendix addressing those three points, we'll circulate internally and aim to return signed within two weeks.

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Orbitlytics
